paragraphs.title: The Queen of Sheba Visits Jerusalem

answers: The queen of Sheba
The queen of Egypt
The wife of Huram
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon.”
easy.q: Who heard of Solomon’s fame and came to Jerusalem?

answers: To build the temple
To prove him with hard questions
To appoint him king
easy.explanation: She came “to prove Solomon with hard questions.”
easy.q: Why did the queen of Sheba come to Solomon?

answers: Weapons and horses
Bread and water
Spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones
easy.explanation: Her camels carried spices, abundant gold, and precious stones.
easy.q: What did the queen’s camels carry?

answers: He told her all her questions
He sent her away
He asked her for more gifts
medium.explanation: Solomon told her all her questions, and nothing was hidden from him.
medium.q: What did Solomon do when the queen spoke with him?

answers: Only his army
His house, table, servants, apparel, and ascent to the LORD’s house
Only his treasures
medium.explanation: She saw his house, table, servants, their apparel, cupbearers, and his ascent to the house of the LORD.
medium.q: What did the queen see in Jerusalem besides Solomon’s wisdom?

answers: She became very angry
She immediately left
She was overwhelmed and had no strength left
medium.explanation: The expression shows that she was deeply astonished by what she saw and heard.
medium.q: What does “there was no more spirit in her” mean?

answers: To test whether his reported wisdom was true
To teach him her own wisdom
To ask him to build her a palace
challenge.explanation: She came specifically to prove Solomon with difficult questions.
challenge.q: Why did the queen bring hard questions to Solomon?

answers: She cared only about Solomon’s wealth
She admired his wisdom, order, service, and worship
She wanted to remain in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The passage describes her admiration for Solomon’s wisdom, household, servants, and worship.
challenge.q: What does the list of things the queen saw reveal about her impression?

answers: His wisdom drew her from far away to test him
His wisdom kept her from speaking with him
His wisdom caused her to take his treasures
challenge.explanation: She heard of his fame, traveled to Jerusalem, and tested him with questions.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between Solomon’s wisdom and the queen’s visit?

answers: It was false
It was true
It was too small to matter
easy.explanation: She said, “It was a true report which I heard in mine own land.”
easy.q: What did the queen say about the report she had heard in her own land?

answers: Half of his wisdom had not been told to her
His wisdom was less than reported
He could not answer her questions
easy.explanation: She said that “the one half of the greatness” of his wisdom had not been told to her.
easy.q: What did the queen discover after seeing Solomon?

answers: Only horses and chariots
A house in Jerusalem
Gold, spices, and precious stones
easy.explanation: She gave him one hundred and twenty talents of gold, abundant spices, and precious stones.
easy.q: What did the queen give Solomon?

answers: Because God had set Solomon on his throne to do judgment and justice
Because God gave her Solomon’s treasures
Because God made her ruler over Jerusalem
medium.explanation: She blessed the LORD for setting Solomon on the throne and making him king to do judgment and justice.
medium.q: Why did the queen bless the LORD?

answers: The abundance and greatness of Solomon’s wisdom
The distance between two kingdoms
The number of Solomon’s servants
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the great extent of Solomon’s wisdom.
medium.q: What does “the greatness of thy wisdom” emphasize?

answers: He kept everything for himself
He gave her all her desire and what she asked
He returned all the gifts
medium.explanation: Solomon gave her all her desire, whatever she asked, besides what she had brought.
medium.q: How did Solomon respond to the queen’s gifts?

answers: She connected the king’s greatness with God’s blessing
She believed Solomon was not wise
She wanted to replace Israel’s worship
challenge.explanation: She praised Solomon’s wisdom and blessed the LORD who had placed him on the throne.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the queen praising both Solomon and the LORD?

answers: The report was greatly exaggerated
The reality surpassed what she had heard
She refused to believe what she saw
challenge.explanation: She said that the report was true, yet even half of Solomon’s greatness had not been told.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between the report and what the queen saw emphasize?

answers: It involved mutual honor and royal fellowship
It was a military conflict
The queen became Solomon’s servant
challenge.explanation: The queen brought valuable gifts, and Solomon gave her what she desired.
challenge.q: What does the exchange of gifts show about the meeting?

answers: One hundred and twenty talents
Six hundred and threescore and six talents
Three hundred talents
easy.explanation: The weight of gold was six hundred and threescore and six talents.
easy.q: How much gold came to Solomon in one year?

answers: Pure gold
Silver
Brass
easy.explanation: The throne of ivory was overlaid with pure gold.

answers: Six
Twelve
Seven
easy.explanation: The passage says, “there were six steps to the throne.”
easy.q: How many steps led to the throne?

answers: Two hundred targets and three hundred shields
Three hundred targets and two hundred shields
Six hundred targets and one hundred shields
medium.explanation: Solomon made two hundred targets and three hundred shields of beaten gold.
medium.q: How many targets and shields did Solomon make?

answers: Gold shaped or worked into objects
Gold that had no value
Gold hidden behind a gate
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to gold worked into the targets and shields.
medium.q: What does “beaten gold” describe in this passage?

answers: In the house of the forest of Lebanon
In the city of David
On the ships of Tarshish
medium.explanation: The king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
medium.q: Where did Solomon place the targets and shields?

answers: The throne’s splendor and royal dignity
The danger of wild animals in Jerusalem
Solomon’s skill as a hunter
challenge.explanation: The lions contribute to the throne’s impressive royal appearance.
challenge.q: What does the description of lions around the throne emphasize?

answers: The throne was plain and ordinary
The throne was unique and extraordinarily impressive
Solomon had no royal throne
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the throne’s unmatched magnificence.
challenge.q: What does “There was not the like made in any kingdom” imply?

answers: Silver was unavailable in the kingdom
The abundance of wealth made silver seem insignificant
The king forbade the use of silver
challenge.explanation: The statement portrays the extraordinary wealth of Solomon’s reign.
challenge.q: What does it mean that silver was “not any thing accounted of” in Solomon’s days?

answers: With the servants of Huram
With the queen of Sheba
With the kings of Arabia
easy.explanation: The king’s ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram.
easy.q: With whom did Solomon’s ships go to Tarshish?

answers: Once a year
Once every three years
Once every ten years
easy.explanation: The ships came “every three years once.”
easy.q: How often did the ships of Tarshish come?

answers: Riches and wisdom
The number of his sons
The size of his palace only
easy.explanation: Solomon passed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
easy.q: In what did Solomon surpass all the kings of the earth?

answers: Gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks
Only cedar and stone
Bread, water, and tools
medium.explanation: The ships brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
medium.q: What did the ships of Tarshish bring?

answers: Musical instruments
Animals brought as gifts
Silver vessels
medium.explanation: Mules are listed among the horses and gifts brought to Solomon.
medium.q: What were mules in this passage?

answers: To hear the wisdom God had put in his heart
To take his throne
To build his house
medium.explanation: They came to hear Solomon’s wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
medium.q: Why did the kings of the earth seek Solomon’s presence?

answers: They brought him wealth, rare goods, and contact with many rulers
They caused him to give up his kingdom
They prevented him from ruling Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The passage describes ships, valuable goods, royal gifts, horses, and increasing riches.
challenge.q: How did trade and gifts contribute to Solomon’s greatness?

answers: The kings brought gifts when they came to hear his wisdom
The gifts were meant to teach Solomon wisdom
The kings brought gifts only after Solomon died
challenge.explanation: The kings sought Solomon to hear his wisdom and brought each man his present.
challenge.q: What connection is made between Solomon’s wisdom and the gifts from the kings?

answers: They included trade in valuable and unusual goods
They were limited to one city
The ships were used only for fishing
challenge.explanation: Gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks show the wide range of his trade.
challenge.q: What does the variety of goods brought by the ships show about Solomon’s connections?

paragraphs.title: Solomon’s Kingdom and the End of His Reign

answers: Thirty years
Forty years
Seventy years
easy.explanation: Solomon reigned over all Israel forty years.
easy.q: How many years did Solomon reign in Jerusalem?

answers: In the city of David his father
In the house of the forest of Lebanon
In Egypt
easy.explanation: He was buried in the city of David his father.

answers: Jeroboam the son of Nebat
Rehoboam his son
Huram
easy.explanation: Rehoboam, Solomon’s son, reigned in his stead.

answers: In the book of Nathan, the prophecy of Ahijah, and the visions of Iddo
Only in the records of the kings of Arabia
Only in the writings of the queen of Sheba
medium.explanation: The passage refers to Nathan, Ahijah, and Iddo as sources for Solomon’s other acts.
medium.q: Where were the rest of Solomon’s acts written?

answers: A prophet or visionary
A merchant
A military commander
medium.explanation: A seer is one who receives or declares prophetic visions.
medium.q: What is a “seer” in the phrase “Iddo the seer”?

answers: Solomon reigned, died and was buried, and Rehoboam succeeded him
Rehoboam reigned before Solomon was born
Solomon was buried before he became king
medium.explanation: The passage ends with Solomon’s reign, death, burial, and Rehoboam’s succession.
medium.q: What was the sequence of events at the end of the chapter?

answers: To refer readers to records of Solomon’s other acts
To say that all Solomon’s acts were forgotten
To claim that the queen of Sheba wrote the chapter
challenge.explanation: The passage directs readers to sources containing the rest of Solomon’s acts.
challenge.q: Why does the passage mention the writings of prophets and seers?

answers: The kingdom passed to Solomon’s son after his death
Rehoboam ruled before Solomon
Solomon gave up the throne during his lifetime
challenge.explanation: After Solomon died and was buried, Rehoboam reigned in his stead.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the transition from Solomon to Rehoboam?

answers: By describing his reign, death, burial, and succession by his son
By describing only one battle
By describing only the queen’s visit
challenge.explanation: The conclusion includes Solomon’s forty-year reign, burial, and Rehoboam’s succession.
challenge.q: How does the chapter summarize Solomon’s period?
